Source slide page 1 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Introduction to Python Imaging Library (PIL)

UE25CS151A
Department of Computer Science and Engineering

Prof. Kundhavai K R, CSE Department

Source slide page 2 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Introduction to PIL (Pillow)

What is PIL/Pillow?
Pillow = modern version of Python Imaging Library (PIL) 
Used for: 
Opening images Editing images Saving images (multiple formats)

[Image text, OCR]
pillow

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Introduction to PIL (Pillow)

Why use Pillow?
Easy to use Supports many formats (JPEG, PNG, BMP, GIF, TIFF, …) Great for resizing, cropping, rotating, filtering images 
Install Pillow
pip install pillow

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Importing & Loading an Image

Load an Image
from PIL import Image
img = Image.open("PES LOGO.jpg")
img.show()

Supported Formats
JPEG, PNG, BMP, GIF, TIFF, and more.

Output:

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Basic Image Information

print(img.format)   # e.g., JPEG
print(img.size)     # (width, height)
print(img.mode)     # RGB, RGBA, L etc.

Meaning
format: file type size: pixel dimensions mode: color channels

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Resizing Images

Resizing Images
resized_img = img.resize((200, 200))
resized_img.show()

Note - resize() returns a new image and may distort aspect ratio.
To maintain aspect ratio:
img.thumbnail((200, 200))
img.show()

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Converting Image Modes

Converting Image Modes
gray_img = img.convert("L")
gray_img.show()
Common Modes:
1 → Black & white (1-bit) L → Grayscale (8-bit) RGB → Color (3 channels) RGBA → Color + Transparency CMYK → Printing format

Source slide page 8 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Saving, Rotating and Cropping Images

Saving Images
gray_img.save("output_image.png")
 Rotating : rotate(degrees)
rotated_img = img.rotate(45)
rotated_img.show()
Cropping : Image.crop(left, upper, right, lower) pixel coordinates
cropped_img = img.crop((50, 50, 200, 200))
cropped_img.show()

Source slide page 9 (extracted text):

Department of Computer Science and Engineering

NOTES.text:
Transcript block 1 (source interval 000000-000299 seconds):
[00:00:00.836] Hello everyone and welcome. Today we are going to explore Pillow, the modern version of Python Imaging Library, also called PIL.
[00:00:15.588] Simple and powerful library that helps us open images, edit images, and save images in multiple formats.
[00:00:29.060] It specially deals with image processing tasks. Let's begin.
[00:00:37.796] Pillow is widely used because it is easy to understand, support many image formats, and includes built-in functions for tasks like resizing, cropping, rotating and filtering images. To install Pillow module, we simply use Pip install pillow.
[00:01:08.740] To start with below, we first import the image class. So image is a class here. Here's a basic code to open an image and display it on the screen.
[00:01:21.572] So for that, image class open function lets you to open the image that is there in the argument. Image.show displays it using your system's default viewer.
[00:01:38.116] Pillow supports JPEG, PNG, BMP, JIF, TIF, and many more image formats. So this example is importing the image class and using the functions open and show.
[00:01:59.108] Once we load the image, we can check some important details like format, which tells the file type like JPEG, or GIF, or Tiv, etc. Then the size, which gives the width and height in pixels.
[00:02:19.524] Then the mode shows the colour representation such as RGB or grayscale.
[00:02:29.828] These properties help us understand the image before processing it.
[00:02:38.212] Resizing is one of the most common operations in image processing. Here's how we resize an image.
[00:02:49.988] So this resize function resizes the image to a given dimension. But it may distort the aspect ratio.
[00:03:06.820] To maintain the aspect ratio we can use thumbnail. This ensures the image is resized without stretching or squashing.
[00:03:21.572] converting the image modes. You can use convert function
[00:03:29.380] to convert to an image to a different colour mode. The common colour modes are one, which is pure black and white, it's just one bit. So zero stands for black, one stands for white.
[00:03:49.796] L, which is grayscale. All the shades of gray colour will be represented in an 8-bit representation. Then RGB, red, green, blue colour, three channels, and this is also an 8-bit representation.
[00:04:09.732] RGBA.
[00:04:13.732] Red, green, blue, and A stands for alpha, which is represents the transparency. Then C M Y K, which stands for Syan, Majenta, Low, and Black.
[00:04:31.812] Mostly used in printing.
[00:04:35.908] Mode conversion is especially useful in machine learning preprocessing, where special formats are required.
[00:04:46.340] Next one, let's take a look into few more essential operations like saving images. To save an image that you have worked on, you can use save function. Then to rotate an image, you can use rotate function and give the degrees as argument.

Transcript block 2 (source interval 000300-000599 seconds):
[00:05:05.828] To crop an image, we can use crop function and the syntaxes you can give the pixel coordinates as left, upper, right, lower to extract the specific region from the image.
[00:05:24.996] These operations make Pillow extremely useful for automation workflows, image editing tasks, and pre processing pipelines.
[00:05:37.700] Thank you. To summarize, Pillow is a very powerful and big enough friendly Python library for image processing. We learned how to use open images, display them, resize, convert color modes, rotate, crop and save images.
[00:05:57.156] With these foundations you can build a wide variety of image based applications from simple editors to machine learning pipelines. Thank you for watching and happy coding.
